sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-code heritage; French-influenced commercial code and Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; EU law prevails in AML/CFT and company-law harmonization)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU network of more than 100 bilateral investment treaties concluded by the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union
US-Luxembourg Income Tax Treaty of 1996 as amended by the 2009 Protocol; DTAA network with approximately 80 jurisdictions (including China, Singapore, UAE, Germany)
EU-wide trade instruments: CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU Directives on Merger Taxation, Interest & Royalties, and Parent-Subsidiary (as transposed)
ICSID Convention of 1965 membership and New York Convention of 1958 on enforcement of arbitral awards

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (consolidated, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing EU Directive AMLD5 and by subsequent AMLD6 amendments); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and the related Grand-Ducal implementing regulations; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on professional due diligence obligations; Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade register (RCS); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (LSC).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (with regulated-professional access on a legitimate-interest basis for obliged entities under the Law of 13 January 2019, as restricted after the CJEU WM case; no unrestricted public access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder and each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or competent consulate of the country of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record extract for each manager or authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the person's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised proof of residential address (utility bill or recent bank statement for each UBO/manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank in the country of residence, with notarial certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each shareholder contributing capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the shareholder in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence / current company extract where a legal person appears in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (EU/EEA public documents may benefit from Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 exemption)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and authorised signatories against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iii) OFAC SDN list where USD payment rails are used; and (iv) the national Luxembourg financial sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Finance. PEP definition follows FATF Recommendations and AMLD5/AMLD6 as implemented by the Law of 12 November 2004; domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, plus family members and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence, independent senior-management approval, source-of-wealth documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any positive sanctions or PEP hit triggers immediate filing of a suspicious-transaction report with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) and refusal or suspension of the incorporation mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS e-Filing portal at www.lbr.lu; name clearance obtained via the 'certificat de non-conformité' (negative certificate) issued by the RCS
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are made in French; the legal-form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' is mandatory; names must be in Latin script only, with non-Latin names transliterated into Latin characters and supported by a certified transliteration; names must be unique, non-misleading, compliant with public order, and must not contain protected professional designation terms not held by the applicant.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS rejection, the applicant may (i) re-file online with a corrected name through the LBR portal (processing typically within 2-5 business days); (ii) request a formal negative certificate where the defect relates to identity or conformity; and (iii) appeal the refusal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (civil chamber) within 3 months of notification under the Code of Civil Procedure, represented by a Luxembourg avocat, with the State Prosecutor's office served as respondent. Filing an appeal does not suspend the name queue, so a parallel corrective re-filing is advisable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted with strict substance conditions: the SARL must maintain a physical registered office in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (Law of 10 August 1915, art. 9, and Law of 19 December 2002), which may be provided by a licensed domiciliation agent under the Law of 1 August 2007 on the freedom of establishment; corporate records, minutes, and accounting documentation must be physically accessible in Luxembourg and management decisions must be traceable to local directors. For an online cosmetics DTC business using Shopify Payments and PayPal, hosting and payment-platform contracts may remain abroad, but the entity must evidence Luxembourg as the place of effective management; a pure mailbox address without any local mandate is rejected by the RCS and by banks applying JSF/CSSF expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 5-10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a low AML-risk online retailer with clean registration and compliant UBO filing; the probability rises to roughly 15-25% over years 1-3 where the entity relies exclusively on domiciliation without documented local substance (board minutes, local accounting, director presence); inspections may be conducted by the Luxembourg tax administration under LIR art. 62, by RBE verification authorities, and by CSSF inspectors where the company is a regulated professional.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance / negative certificate ('certificat de non-conformité') via LBR e-formality
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fee schedule; nominal fee, often bundled with notarial disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif SARL, including disbursements and filing coordination)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under the 21 May 1994 arrêté; minimum scale on EUR 12,000 share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration duty on capital contributions ('droit d'apport' at 1% of subscribed capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory 1% capital duty under the Law of 14 March 1920 on registration duties
Statutory fee schedule under the Law of 19 December 2002

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation extract in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff for standard company announcements
Gratuitous mandatory filing within one month of incorporation under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization costs for KYC bundle (passport copies, address proof, police records, bank references for all shareholders/UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the document's country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, notaries, consulates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-document tariffs (USD 20-30 per document, estimated 5-8 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French or German translation of foreign KYC and supporting documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per-page translation tariff (small documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation service for the first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 1,800-2,500 per year for a low-risk DTC e-commerce entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate secretarial and AML/KYC coordination support (notary file, RBE filing, bank account introduction, ongoing compliance framework)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Professional corporate service provider under PFS rules or Luxembourg legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for a standard SARL formation package with banking onboarding support

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Title VI, Articles 710-1 to 710-24, governing the société à responsabilité limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Luxembourg Business Registers; Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant and industrialist.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with mandatory notarial intervention by a Luxembourg civil-law notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association, followed by RCS registration through the Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000 and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be deposited and blocked in a bank account opened with a Luxembourg credit institution in the name of the company being formed, or held in notarial escrow, and evidenced by a bank blocking certificate or notary receipt before the deed is signed; in-kind contributions must be fully vested and, when required, valued by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d’entreprises). The blocked funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators accept the subscription of the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into [NUMBER] shares of EUR [VALUE] each, fully subscribed, with cash contributions deposited in a blocked bank account or notarial escrow until registration; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be [ADDRESS], Luxembourg; RESOLVED, that [NAME] be appointed manager, with sole or joint signature authority; RESOLVED, that the manager be authorized to sign all registration forms, declarations and publications with the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax administration and social security authorities; RESOLVED, that all prior incorporation acts are ratified. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and pre-incorporation documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS pre-search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify availability of the proposed company name through the RCS online database; instruct the notary to prepare the draft articles of association, share subscription list and beneficial ownership information; secure the registered office address and obtain written consent from the owner of the premises.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of shareholders and managers
Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) for each manager
Bank references or evidence of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or unavailable, instruct the notary to submit alternative names and rerun the RCS pre-search before the deed is drafted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share capital deposit and blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company to be incorporated; ensure each subscriber transfers the agreed cash contribution; obtain an attestation de blocage confirming the credited amount and blocking until RCS registration; if contributions in kind are involved, arrange statutory valuation and a réviseur d’entreprises report where required.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking certificate or notary escrow receipt
Valuation report for in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide bank statements and source-of-wealth evidence; if the bank still refuses, transfer the funds to the notary’s escrow account in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend before the Luxembourg notary and sign the authenticated deed of incorporation; appoint the manager and authorized signatories; approve the articles of association; pay notarial fees and registration taxes; the notary then e-files the deed with the RCS and prepares the legal publication.
required_dossiers: Capital blocking certificate or escrow receipt
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies between the statutes and the capital evidence, amend the draft documents and schedule a new deed execution; any additional drafting fees are settled before the new appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed together with the RCS registration application form; pay the statutory registration fee; the RCS verifies the legal form, registered office, managers and corporate purpose; once admitted, the company acquires legal personality and receives its RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees
Beneficial owner declaration for the RBE register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification notice, submit corrected documents within the 15-day statutory window; if the application is erroneously rejected, file a formal request for ex officio registration or an administrative appeal through counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and official RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the official RCS extract; the RCS publishes the mandatory incorporation particulars in the RESA electronic compendium; verify the extract accurately states the legal form, share capital, managers, registered office and corporate purpose; use the extract as definitive proof of incorporation for banks and counterparties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, submit a rectification application to the RCS and ensure the corrected RESA announcement is re-issued before using the extract for commercial purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security and EORI registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l’Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDTV); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration des Douanes et Accises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL with the ACD for corporate income tax and obtain the national business number; submit the VAT registration form through MyGuichet or the AEDTV if taxable supplies are made in Luxembourg or intra-EU distance sales of cosmetics commence; register with the CCSS for social security and work-accident coverage; apply for an EORI number if goods will be imported into the EU.
required_dossiers: VAT and national business number forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration queries the registration, provide the RCS extract and a certified copy of the deed; for VAT, filing a corrective return or an appeal to the AEDTV within three months cures most formal defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des PME) via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for the establishment authorization before commencing online retail sales; evidence professional qualification or management capacity and provide clean criminal record extracts; the authorization is company-specific and authorizes the declared commercial activity, including distance selling of cosmetics and personal care products.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) for each manager
Evidence of professional qualification or management skills certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry requests further evidence of professional capacity, submit an equivalency ruling or a management skills certificate; if the authorization is refused, appeal to the Minister of the Economy within the statutory time limit and, alternatively, to the administrative tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation compliance and operational license trigger review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Corps Grand-Ducal d’Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); Administration de l’Environnement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration in the RBE register within one month; activate a commercial bank account and release the blocked capital after registration; notify the ITM before the first employee is hired; if a physical warehouse or storage area is established, obtain fire safety clearance from CGDIS and verify whether environmental classing is required; for cosmetics placed on the market, ensure compliance with Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products.
required_dossiers: Fire safety and structural load certificates, if premises are used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late beneficial ownership filings, file promptly and prepare to pay the administrative fine; for fire or environmental queries, coordinate remediation with CGDIS and the Administration de l’Environnement before any operational use of the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des PME) / MyGuichet.lu
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral industrial operating license is required for pure online retail of finished cosmetics; the general business establishment authorization (autorisation d’établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 remains mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA required for online retail and distribution of finished cosmetics; if warehousing of finished goods exceeds statutory thresholds, a class 4 declaration may be required before commencement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a pure e-commerce activity. If a warehouse is operating, general waste producer obligations apply under the Law of 21 March 2017 and packaging producer-responsibility rules apply to shipped cosmetic products; no industrial wastewater or VOC discharge is expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety clearance is required for a purely administrative registered office. Any warehouse or premises open to employees must pass a fire safety inspection by the Corps Grand-Ducal d’Incendie et de Secours, provide structural load certificates if racking is installed, and be declared to the Inspection du Travail et des Mines before the first employee is engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for indirect taxes; official multichannel portal: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu; company register interface: rcs.lbr.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Notarized incorporation deed of the SARL (minimum share capital EUR 12,000; at least 25% paid up); 2) Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) within 1 month of deed execution to obtain the national business identification number (matricule, 11-digit); 3) The RCS online filing automatically notifies the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax purposes and the AED for VAT; the taxpayer receives the direct tax file number and the Luxembourg VAT number (format LU + 8 digits) through MyGuichet; 4) Filing of the beneficial ownership (RBE) declaration within 1 month; 5) Non-resident shareholders or directors must present certified identification and a local registered office address; no economic-substance filing is required at registration stage, but substance documentation is expected for future tax treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - A Luxembourg SARL is fully opaque and resident for tax purposes; taxable on worldwide income under Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; no pass-through or check-the-box option is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg. Available statutory elections: (1) fiscal integration (tax consolidation) under Art. 164bis LIR for Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries held at least 95%; (2) VAT grouping as a single taxable person under Art. 59 of the VAT Code for financially, economically and organisationally integrated resident entities; (3) election of the 80% IP-box exemption under Art. 50bis LIR; (4) election of a tax year-end other than 31 December; (5) binding rulings with the ACD on business models and transfer pricing; anti-hybrid rules (ATAD) are mandatory, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA) pursuant to the Luxembourg VAT Code, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No domestic de minimis turnover threshold: any person carrying on an independent economic activity in Luxembourg is registrable from the first euro. For EU distance sales into Luxembourg, the union-wide threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (Art. 59bis VAT Code), above which the OSS regime applies. For imports of low-value consignments not exceeding EUR 150, the IOSS regime is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no dedicated e-invoicing clearance API and no digital stamping obligation for private B2B/B2C transactions. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to public procurement (PEPPOL/Peppol BIS). Standard EU invoicing rules apply (Art. 75-77 VAT Code), including sequential numbering, audit trail and a 10-year archiving obligation. Physical point-of-sale retail in Luxembourg may be subject to the certified electronic cash register requirement (Law of 19 December 2020), but the pure online DTC flow using Shopify Payments / PayPal does not trigger that POS cash-register obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (1) direct exports of goods where transport is carried out by the supplier or on its behalf to a destination outside the EU (Art. 42 VAT Code), provided the goods leave the EU within 90 days after supply and the exporter holds proof of export before the VAT return is filed; (2) intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered customers with valid VAT ID and EC sales list (Art. 43 VAT Code); (3) supplies of digital services to non-EU customers falling outside the Luxembourg territorial scope. A Luxembourg beauty DTC retailer may zero-rate cross-border parcel sales to non-EU consumers; sales to EU consumers are distance sales, not zero-rated, and are taxed at destination via OSS or IOSS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ETN/EX formalities with MRN, including the parcel exporter declaration for e-commerce shipments)
Bill of Lading / CMR / Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment proof (SWIFT MT103 / gateway settlement report) evidencing consideration from the foreign buyer
Proof of customer identity and delivery confirmation for cross-border DTC parcels
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may retrospectively claw back zero-rating and assess Luxembourg VAT at 17% if the export documentation is deficient or the goods do not leave the EU within the statutory window. Late payment interest and a monthly late-payment surcharge of 1% up to a maximum of 10% apply (Art. 48 VAT Code). Fraudulent claims attract administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 and, in the case of intentional evasion, criminal sanctions including imprisonment up to 5 years. The ACD/AED may also re-characterise artificial arrangements under Luxembourg's abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. 6 Steueranpassungsgesetz), adding a 10% penalty and the full clawback of any VAT refunded. Although Luxembourg VAT law does not impose an explicit 180-day FX repatriation deadline, the AED treats export receivables outstanding beyond 180 days as an audit red flag and may require additional commercial substantiation of the transaction's genuine export nature.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is part of the eurozone and the EU single market; both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible under Articles 63-65 TFEU. There are no exchange control restrictions, no FDI screening, and no profit remittance hurdles for non-resident shareholders beyond standard Luxembourg withholding tax (15% general dividend withholding, reduced to 0% / 5% under participation exemption or tax treaty) and supporting documentation of beneficial ownership. Foreign currency accounts with no position limits are freely permitted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio exists for export proceeds in Luxembourg. Exporters may retain balances in any currency; only statistical reporting thresholds to BCL balance of payments and CSSF AML/CFT reporting apply. No statutory repatriation timeline is imposed by law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for EU/EEA-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) that hold a licence recognized in Luxembourg under PSD2, including local CSSF-licensed EMIs and EEA passporting EMIs. Offshore (non-EEA) EMIs may not provide services to the SARL without a Luxembourg branch or an authorized payment institution representative office; reverse solicitation is applied narrowly and creates a legal risk. For digital commerce, EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, and multi-currency PSPs are feasible if they maintain segregated safeguarding accounts and full AML/KYC acceptance. Maintain a tier-1 resident bank settlement account as the primary treasury account and use the EMI only for e-commerce collection and disbursement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of the statutory manager (gérant) and the ultimate beneficial owner is generally required for opening tier-1 commercial bank accounts in Luxembourg. The CSSF AML circular permits a degree of non-face-to-face onboarding through audio-video identification, but banks usually mandate an in-person interview at the branch or a Luxembourg registered agent to complete due diligence, especially for holding structures. Remote opening is more flexibly offered by EU-regulated EMIs, but still requires certified copies, survey documents, and a bank reference. A registered address in Luxembourg and valid local business licence (RCS registration) are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity with non-EU entity or trust in a tax-favourable offshore jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an updated corporate organisation chart, Luxembourg RCS extract, certified copies of passports and proof of address of each beneficial owner, a signed Luxembourg beneficial owner declaration (LBR), and local counsel legal opinion on source of funds and wealth (audited financial statements or notarized capital proof).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of e-commerce payments from cross-border third-party platforms (PayPal/Shopify) triggering transaction monitoring and potentially unexplained wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit platform settlement reports, payment provider contract, order-level transaction log summary, chargeback statement, inventory and shipping documents (CMR/invoices), tax registration numbers, and a three-month cash-flow forecast; adopt an automated AML transaction monitoring process under CSSF guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from an unregulated third country or high-risk jurisdiction for the SARL's minimum capital deposit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the notarized capital deposit certificate issued by a Luxembourg bank, source-of-funds statement from the transferring financial institution, passport and ownership documentation, and a sworn statement from the board that the capital is free of any criminal origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity classified as 'online retail of cosmetics' with potential red flags for parallel trading, counterfeit supply, or sanctioned-country exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide supplier certificates of origin, INCI/CPNP compliance documents, EU responsible person contracts, and evidence of trade sanctions screening on customers and supply chain (e.g., integrated sanctions filtering and negative media screening).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Incoming shareholder capital contributions must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank account to the SARL's resident bank account, using ISO 20022 external purpose code 'EQUI' (equity). The remittance must reference the notarial deed of capital increase, the RCS registration number, and the bank's required beneficiary identification. Verification includes the bank's 'notice of inward remittance', the RCS updated capital certificate, and confirmation of proper VAT/CRS/AML checks. For EU-originated payments, SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant is acceptable for amounts under €100k, with purpose code 'BEXP' if not classified as equity; nevertheless, direct capital subscriptions must clearly state 'EQUI'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments in euros are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant for settlement; for non-euro currencies, SWIFT MT103 is the primary clean payment rail worldwide. For larger inventory purchases, a commercial letter of credit (sight or deferred) issued through BGL/BCEE may be used, requiring the supplier's draft and complying documents. Shopify/PayPal disbursements settle to the SARL's resident bank account via standard collection rails. All outbound payments must be reconciled against underlying invoices, Incoterms and trade documentation, and respect the anti-money-laundering payment thresholds requiring EU Automated Reporting on cross-border transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) with maturities up to 24 months
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with capital controls or transfer restrictions (e.g., offshore RMB, certain Asian currencies)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS/CIRS) aligned with EURIBOR or €STR benchmarks
Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars, entered into with board-approved counterparties under EMIR/MiFID II

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, and statutory auditor's report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The general meeting must approve the annual accounts within 6 months after the financial year-end; the approved accounts must be filed with the RCS within 1 month after approval. For a calendar-year SARL this means approval by 30 June and filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The public prosecutor or the RCS may seek a court order compelling filing under penalty; directors or managers may face fines and coercive daily penalties; persistent failure to file may trigger the administrative dissolution and strike-off procedure under the Law on Luxembourg Business Registers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation and updated UBO declaration if the shareholding has changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The confirmation must be filed during the calendar anniversary month of the entity's RCS registration; any substantive change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the company becoming aware of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation or updated declaration may result in administrative fines and criminal sanctions under the amended Luxembourg UBO Law; repeated non-compliance is treated as an AML governance deficiency and may block certain corporate transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual corporate tax return is due by 31 December of the following year; non-calendar fiscal periods must be filed within 5 months after the period end unless the ACD grants an extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to default assessments issued by the ACD, late-payment interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid tax, and administrative fines; deliberate non-filing may attract tax-evasion penalties and criminal prosecution, but a tax default alone does not directly trigger RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT periodic returns (monthly or quarterly statutory return; not an annual franchise filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg Indirect Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: VAT returns are due by the 15th day of the month following the reporting period; the final VAT position for the calendar year is reconciled in the last period's return of the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT returns and late VAT payments trigger late-filing and late-interest penalties under Luxembourg VAT law; continued default may lead to enforced collection and seizure of assets, but it does not in itself cause administrative strike-off from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL is required to have an independent statutory audit if, at the balance-sheet date in two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet over EUR 4,400,000; net turnover over EUR 8,800,000; average staff count of more than 50. Statutory audit is also mandatory without the size test for public-interest entities, regulated financial undertakings, and where required by the articles of association, shareholders, or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts are prepared under Luxembourg GAAP as derived from the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and applicable Grand-Ducal regulations implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU. Small undertakings may use abridged formats and reduced disclosure; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is available for individual accounts by option and is mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation in the RBE during the anniversary month of its RCS registration. The confirmation records that the beneficial owner data on file remains accurate. Any share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be declared to the RBE within 1 month of the company becoming aware of the change; this obligation survives the annual confirmation and applies to every movement in the shareholder register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of general meetings and management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–3,200 per year for registered office, corporate domiciliation, and corporate secretarial services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500–12,000 per year for a statutory audit of a small retail SARL prepared under Lux GAAP; a reduced review engagement may fall in the USD 3,500–6,000 range if no full audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (up to 8% for certain assets), participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, notional interest deduction (NID) for equity financing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and Form 1001 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via eCDF (Electronic Corporate Tax Filing) or MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions available upon request (typically to 31 December).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification details (name, address, RCS number, tax ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax ID and registered office address; if non-resident, indicate permanent establishment details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the fiscal year covered; for non-residents, align with Luxembourg tax year.
Compute Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions if applicable.
Claim foreign tax credits under DTA; attach TRC and supporting documentation.
Disclose any TP adjustments; attach TP documentation if thresholds met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 per month (max €2,500); late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties up to 10% of tax due for gross negligence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced WHT under a DTA, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the residence state and a Form 105 (Luxembourg withholding tax exemption request) to the Luxembourg tax administration before the dividend payment. For EU parent-subsidiary directive, a 0% rate applies if the parent holds at least 10% for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions met); Interest: statutory 15% (reduced to 0% under EU directive or DTA, typically 0-10% under treaties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million group consolidated turnover and EUR 1 million entity turnover trigger Local File; Master File required if group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in certain activities (e.g., holding, financing, IP). For a retail company, ESR is not directly applicable, but general substance requirements (office, staff, decision-making) must be met to avoid being classified as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false invoicing, or concealment of taxable transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; additional tax surcharges up to 100% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No physical presence, no employees, no real business activity, or artificial arrangements to avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; penalties up to EUR 25,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fines and restitution; potential criminal charges for fraud if intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; travel bans may be imposed during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; civil liability for damages.
